questions.q: What problem does a ConfigMap solve for Northbridge's product-catalog service?
options: It encrypts sensitive database credentials
It externalizes non-sensitive configuration from the container image, so the same image can run with different settings in different environments
It automatically scales the number of Pod replicas
It replaces the need for a Service to reach the Pod
questions.explain: A ConfigMap holds key-value configuration separately from the image, letting the same built image run in staging or production with different values injected at deploy time.

questions.q: What does envFrom with a configMapRef do in a Pod spec?
options: Mounts the ConfigMap as a single file
Injects every key in the referenced ConfigMap as an environment variable in the container
Deletes the ConfigMap after the Pod starts
Encrypts the ConfigMap's values at rest
questions.explain: envFrom with configMapRef pulls every key-value pair from the ConfigMap into the container's environment in one block, without listing each variable individually.

questions.q: Northbridge needs to supply a full nginx.conf file to a container rather than a handful of simple key-value settings. What's the better-fit consumption method?
options: envFrom with configMapRef
Mounting the ConfigMap as a volume, where each key becomes a file in the mount path
env with a single valueFrom.configMapKeyRef
ConfigMaps cannot hold file-shaped data
questions.explain: For larger or file-shaped configuration, mounting the ConfigMap as a volume is the better fit — each key in the ConfigMap becomes a file inside the mount path.

questions.q: Northbridge updates a ConfigMap's LOG_LEVEL value while Pods consuming it via envFrom are already running. What happens to those running Pods?
options: They immediately pick up the new LOG_LEVEL value with no restart needed
Nothing changes for environment variables — they were captured once at container start and won't refresh without a Pod restart
The Pods crash immediately when the ConfigMap changes
Kubernetes automatically restarts every Pod using that ConfigMap
questions.explain: Environment variables set via envFrom/env are read once at container startup. A ConfigMap update doesn't retroactively change them — the Pod needs to be restarted (e.g. via a rolling restart) to pick up the new value.

questions.q: Which of these is the correct imperative command to create a ConfigMap from command-line key-value pairs?
options: kubectl apply configmap catalog-config --data LOG_LEVEL=info
kubectl create configmap catalog-config --from-literal=LOG_LEVEL=info
kubectl set configmap catalog-config LOG_LEVEL=info
kubectl create secret catalog-config --from-literal=LOG_LEVEL=info
questions.explain: kubectl create configmap <name> --from-literal=KEY=value is the standard imperative way to create a ConfigMap from literal key-value pairs.
